report.source_text: After the negative PCR results of the CSF acyclovir was stopped. The disturbances in fluid and electrolyte balance were treated with fluid resuscitation and potassium supplementation. Volume repletion was achieved quickly. The patient’s neurological status recovered within 36 hours after the start of ceftriaxone intravenously. Normalisation of sodium levels occurred within 24 hours and potassium levels normalised within 48 hours, after which fluid resuscitation was stopped.

report.source_text: Three days after admittance to the hospital and the start of intravenous antibiotic treatment, the patient had recovered so far that he could be discharged. The stool consistency returned to normal over time. Because of subsiding symptoms in a non-immunocompromised patient, no further antibiotic treatment was found necessary. At a follow-up visit several weeks later, he had recovered fully, except for some memory problems.
report.temporal_cue: 3 days post admission and several weeks follow-up

clinician.trajectory_summary: A 45-year-old HIV-negative MSM presented with acute febrile diarrheal illness (1 day) followed by rapid onset encephalopathy (confusion, disorientation, aphasia) and fever (39.5°C). Initial workup revealed mild CSF pleocytosis (8×10^6 cells/L) with normal glucose and protein, negative bacterial culture, and negative PCR for HSV, VZV, and enterovirus, consistent with encephalopathy rather than meningitis or viral encephalitis. Brain CT excluded structural lesions. Blood cultures were negative. Stool culture confirmed S. flexneri infection sensitive to ceftriaxone. The patient was treated with intravenous ceftriaxone and supportive fluid/electrolyte management. Neurological status recovered within 36 hours of antibiotic initiation, electrolytes normalized within 24-48 hours, and the patient was discharged after 3 days. Follow-up several weeks later showed full recovery with minor residual memory problems.
